contradictions.detail: Dealer stated on the 10/30 video call and again on 11/3 that there are two fobs. The Lemon Squad PPI on 11/2 was presented only one.
Dealer says no tear is visible on the driver bolster. PPI photo 37 shows a tear with yellow foam exposed on the upper outer bolster behind the seatbelt guide.
The description says 'Auburn leather' but the boilerplate line reads 'Interior: Gray'. Photos confirm Auburn.

Listing says service was 'almost exclusively at authorized Mazda dealerships', and the salesperson says Mazda Thousand Oaks 'entire life'. The Carfax shows 2018-2023 work largely at VW Thousand Oaks, apparently the same dealer group.
Listing says $23,540 'includes fees'. The deal sheet shows price $23,470 plus $528.25 in fees and tax, with taxable dealer fees making price-plus-fees $50 above the ad.

critical_evidence.evidence: Oil changes are dated by time in the Carfax, every 6-12 months through 2024, then a 21-month gap explained as storage. No reported brake fluid flush entry in roughly 10 years. The receipt folder exists but has not been shared for this item.

No reported transmission repair or warranty entry in the Carfax. The PPI road test rated gearbox and clutch Good. A Warrantech/Mazda extended protection contract was issued in 12/2016, with no claims history seen. No readable door-jamb build-date photo; the car is a late-2016 build.

PPI cycled the RF roof smoothly and the video showed the roof mechanism area dry. No photos with footwell carpet lifted or of the targa/drain areas. Seat-rail bolts and floor connectors were not examined.

Carfax (as of 10/27/2026) states no open recalls. The airbag control module software recall 24V695000 applies to 2016-2023 MX-5. No specific completion line is seen, so confirm with an NHTSA VIN lookup or a Mazda printout. The automatic-TCM recall 19V072000 does not apply to this manual car.
Dealer claims 2021 tire date codes. The PPI did not record DOT dates and rated the battery Good without a date code. No tire or battery receipts.

documentation.rationale: Both halves are present but incomplete. Identity and terms are strong: VIN matched at PPI, Carfax one-owner with 25 dated records, clean title, smog passed 9/2026, and an OTD sheet, though fees are not itemized. Maintenance evidence is strong on oil and a clean independent PPI with scan data. The time-based items (brake fluid, coolant) have no reported entries, and the receipt folder is withheld in unredacted form.

condition.rationale: The independent PPI is mechanically clean: no codes, monitors complete, no leaks, underbody good, roof cycles, road test all Good. Observed cosmetic and interior defects pull it down: torn driver bolster, cracked or delaminating screen, small door ding, front chips. Brake fluid and coolant age are unknown, and one rear tire is at 5/32.

price_value.rationale: The $23,470 deal-sheet price sits above the $18,826-23,098 fair-value band (mid $20,881). Auction comps and the 49k-mile Launch Edition at $20,000 support the dealer being $2-3k high. Known interior and key items pull value down further, partly offset by the Launch Edition spec.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual RF with a working hard roof for year-round coastal use, one owner, low-risk drivetrain, in California with smog done, and available now. Price is inside the ideal band. The ND1 155 hp engine is the lesser engine, and price discipline is still needed.

logistics.rationale: Costa Mesa is an in-state fly-and-drive up the coast. The PPI is already completed, a deposit holds the car 5-7 days, CA smog is current, and the dealer is responsive.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Hits several of the buyer's top preferences at once: Machine Gray over Auburn Nappa, RF Launch Edition (one of about 1,000), manual, stock, one owner. Held back from 10 by the ND1 engine and an unconfirmed LSD/Bilstein specification.

evidence.mission_note: A stock, one-owner manual RF in the buyer's ideal colours with a clean independent PPI and current CA smog fits the enthusiast-bridge mission and the year-round coastal use case directly. The open points are price and housekeeping (fluids, key, bolster), not mechanical risk.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax establishes one California owner over ~10 years, a clean title, no reported accidents, and 25 dated dealer-group oil and inspection records. The 11/2/2026 Lemon Squad PPI found no codes with monitors complete, no leaks, a sound underbody, a smoothly cycling RF roof, and a clean road test. Observed defects are an exposed-foam tear on the driver outer bolster, a cracked or delaminating infotainment screen, a small door ding with front chips, and only one key fob presented against the dealer's two-fob claim. Time-based maintenance remains open: there is no reported brake fluid or coolant entry, the receipt folder has not been shared unredacted, and tire and battery date codes are dealer-claimed only after a ~21-month low-use storage period. The $23,470 deal-sheet price is above the computed fair-value band of $18,826-23,098. Auction comps, including a 49k-mile Launch Edition at $20,000, indicate the dealer premium is larger than usual. The specification (Launch Edition, Machine Gray over Auburn, manual) matches the buyer's stated preferences closely, though it carries the 155 hp ND1 engine.
evidence.next_action: Text Ehren Lemon Squad photo 37 and, in the same message, request scans of any brake fluid and coolant receipts, tire DOT and battery date-code photos, and a photo of both fobs, so all of it is in hand before naming a counteroffer.
